name: Set 5: Champions & Chommies
description: Olympic Gold, Motorsport, Iconic Inventions & Braai Customs

questions.q: What is the standard unit of currency used in the United Kingdom?
questions.fact: Pound Sterling (£).

questions.q: How many centimeters are there in a standard meter?
questions.fact: 100 centimeters = 1 meter.

questions.q: What is the traditional ingredient that gives beer its natural fizz and alcohol during fermentation?
questions.fact: Yeast consumes sugars and converts them into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Which popular South African draught beer is famous for the advertising slogan 'Champion Men Deserve Champion Beer'?
questions.fact: Carling Black Label: 'Zamalek' or 'The Black Bull'.

questions.q: How many sides does a standard stop sign have on South African roads?
questions.fact: An eight-sided octagon.

questions.q: In golf, what is the term used for when a player finishes a hole two strokes over par?
questions.fact: One over = Bogey; two over = Double Bogey.

questions.q: What is the common English name for the constellation called the 'Suiderkruis' in Afrikaans?
questions.fact: Crux, depicted on flags of Australia, New Zealand, Brazil, and Samoa.

questions.q: Which popular board game challenges players to solve a murder in Tudor Mansion involving Colonel Mustard and Mrs White?
questions.fact: Created in Birmingham, England by Anthony E. Pratt in 1944.

questions.q: What gas makes up approximately 78% of the Earth's atmosphere?
questions.fact: Nitrogen ~78%, Oxygen ~21%, Argon ~0.9%.

questions.q: Which fruit is dried in the sun to become a raisin?
questions.fact: Sun-dried grapes become raisins (or sultanas).

questions.q: Which South African motorcycle racer won the Moto3 World Championship in 2016 and now competes for Red Bull KTM Factory Racing in MotoGP?
questions.fact: Brad Binder from Krugersdorp: known for his fearless braking and MotoGP race wins.

questions.q: Which South African swimmer stunned the world by defeating Michael Phelps to win Olympic Gold in the 200m butterfly at the 2012 London Olympics?
questions.fact: Chad le Clos won by 0.05 seconds in a dramatic finish.

questions.q: At which iconic South African motorsport circuit outside Johannesburg was the South African Formula One Grand Prix historically held?
questions.fact: Kyalami hosted the South African Grand Prix from 1967 to 1993.

questions.q: Which South African off-road rally driver won the prestigious Dakar Rally in 2009 driving for Volkswagen?
questions.fact: Giniel de Villiers won the 2009 Dakar Rally alongside co-driver Dirk von Zitzewitz.

questions.q: How many gold medals did South African swimming legend Tatjana Smith (Schoenmaker) win across the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Olympic Games?
questions.fact: Gold in 200m breaststroke (Tokyo) and Gold in 100m breaststroke (Paris).

questions.q: In rugby union, what penalty is awarded against a team when a forward intentionally collapses a scrum?
questions.fact: Collapsing a scrum is dangerous play resulting in a full penalty kick.

questions.q: Which legendary rally and circuit driver, known affectionately as 'SuperVan', won 11 South African National Rally Championships?
questions.fact: Sarel van der Merwe: an icon of South African motorsport.

questions.q: In cricket, what is the maximum number of overs a single bowler can bowl in an official 50-over One Day International?
questions.fact: 10 overs per bowler in a 50-over match.

questions.q: Which South African middle-distance runner won Olympic Gold in the women's 800m at both London 2012 and Rio 2016?
questions.fact: Caster Semenya dominated the 800m world stage.

questions.q: What are the five colors of the Olympic rings?
questions.fact: Blue, Yellow, Black, Green, and Red on a white background.

questions.q: In the hit 80s TV series The A-Team, what was B.A. Baracus's greatest fear that required Hannibal to drug him before flights?
questions.round: Round 3 · Action Heroes, Sci-Fi & TV Sitcoms
questions.fact: 'I ain't gettin' on no plane, Hannibal!'

questions.q: Which 1999 sci-fi movie starring Keanu Reeves introduced the iconic slow-motion visual effect known as 'bullet time'?
questions.round: Round 3 · Action Heroes, Sci-Fi & TV Sitcoms
questions.fact: Directed by the Wachowskis, winning 4 Academy Awards.

questions.q: In the sitcom Seinfeld, what holiday was invented by George Costanza's father Frank as an alternative to Christmas?
questions.round: Round 3 · Action Heroes, Sci-Fi & TV Sitcoms
questions.fact: 'Festivus for the rest of us!' Featuring the airing of grievances and feats of strength.

questions.q: Which action star played John Rambo in the First Blood movie series?
questions.round: Round 3 · Action Heroes, Sci-Fi & TV Sitcoms
questions.fact: Sylvester Stallone also co-wrote the screenplay.

questions.q: In Star Wars, what is the name of Han Solo's modified Corellian smuggling spaceship?
questions.round: Round 3 · Action Heroes, Sci-Fi & TV Sitcoms
questions.fact: 'She made the Kessel Run in less than twelve parsecs.'

questions.q: Which television secret agent was famous for disarming bombs using a Swiss Army knife, paperclips, and duct tape?
questions.round: Round 3 · Action Heroes, Sci-Fi & TV Sitcoms
questions.fact: Played by Richard Dean Anderson in the 1985 series.

questions.q: In the animated sitcom The Simpsons, what is Homer Simpson's favorite brand of beer?
questions.round: Round 3 · Action Heroes, Sci-Fi & TV Sitcoms
questions.fact: Served on tap by Moe Szyslak at Moe's Tavern.

questions.q: Who directed the 1993 epic World War II drama Schindler's List?
questions.round: Round 3 · Action Heroes, Sci-Fi & TV Sitcoms
questions.fact: Won seven Academy Awards including Best Director and Best Picture.

questions.q: In the film Braveheart (1995), what famous word does Mel Gibson's character shout before his execution?
questions.round: Round 3 · Action Heroes, Sci-Fi & TV Sitcoms
questions.fact: William Wallace shouting 'Freedom!' with his final breath.

questions.q: What British television comedy featured Rowan Atkinson as a bumbling, silent character driving a green Mini Cooper?
questions.round: Round 3 · Action Heroes, Sci-Fi & TV Sitcoms
questions.fact: First broadcast on ITV in January 1990.

questions.q: What traditional South African bread dough is shaped into round balls and baked directly over the braai grid?
questions.round: Round 4 · Meat on the Coals, Sauces & Breweries
questions.fact: Roosterkoek is baked on the braai grid until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped.

questions.q: What are skewers of marinated lamb or beef cubes interleaved with dried apricots and onions called in South Africa?
questions.round: Round 4 · Meat on the Coals, Sauces & Breweries
questions.fact: From Cape Malay tradition: seasoned with curry, tamarind, and turmeric.

questions.q: Which Namibian beer, brewed under the German Purity Law with only malted barley, hops, and water, is famous across South Africa?
questions.round: Round 4 · Meat on the Coals, Sauces & Breweries
questions.fact: Brewed by Namibia Breweries Limited in Windhoek since 1920.

questions.q: What is the traditional South African sweet confection made of a tart pastry crust filled with baked custard and dusted with cinnamon?
questions.round: Round 4 · Meat on the Coals, Sauces & Breweries
questions.fact: Melktert: smooth, cinnamon-dusted custard perfection.

questions.q: What is the term used in wine tasting for the aroma profile of an aged wine as opposed to a young wine?
questions.round: Round 4 · Meat on the Coals, Sauces & Breweries
questions.fact: Aroma relates to the grape variety; bouquet develops with bottle aging.

questions.q: Which cut of pork spare ribs is characterized by meat attached to the lower breastbone, trimmed into a neat rectangular rack?
questions.round: Round 4 · Meat on the Coals, Sauces & Breweries
questions.fact: St. Louis cut ribs are meatier and flatter than baby backs.

questions.q: What popular South African lager, introduced in 1994, is marketed as low-carb and extra cold?
questions.round: Round 4 · Meat on the Coals, Sauces & Breweries
questions.fact: 'Extra Cold' lager with ice-cold thermochromatic packaging.

questions.q: What sweet jam is traditionally spread inside a braaibroodjie to give it a hint of sweetness against the cheese and onion?
answers: Mrs Ball's Chutney or Apricot jam
questions.round: Round 4 · Meat on the Coals, Sauces & Breweries
questions.fact: Mrs Ball's Chutney or a touch of smooth apricot jam elevates the braaibroodjie.

questions.q: What dark beer style originated in London in the early 18th century as a hearty drink favored by street and river porters?
questions.round: Round 4 · Meat on the Coals, Sauces & Breweries
questions.fact: Named after the street and river porters who loaded cargo along the Thames.

questions.q: What spice gives South African Cape Malay curries, bobotie, and yellow rice their distinctive vibrant yellow color?
questions.round: Round 4 · Meat on the Coals, Sauces & Breweries
questions.fact: Turmeric (known locally as borrie) imparts warm earthy flavor and rich golden color.

questions.q: At which Cape Town hospital did Professor Christiaan Barnard perform the world's first successful human-to-human heart transplant in 1967?
questions.fact: 3 December 1967: recipient Louis Washkansky lived for 18 days with the new heart.

questions.q: Which South African coastal engineering invention, a distinctive geometric 20-ton concrete block, is used worldwide to protect breakwaters from ocean waves?
questions.fact: Invented in East London in 1963 by Eric Merrifield and Aubrey Kruger.

questions.q: Which South African-born physicist shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the development of computer-assisted tomography (CAT scan)?
questions.fact: Allan Cormack attended the University of Cape Town before conducting research at Tufts University.

questions.q: In what calendar year did Apollo 11 astronaut Neil Armstrong become the first human to step onto the surface of the Moon?
questions.fact: 20 July 1969: 'That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.'

questions.q: What ancient trade network linked China and the Mediterranean world for overland silk, spice, and horse trade?
questions.fact: Spanned over 6,400 km across Eurasia.

questions.q: Which British passenger ocean liner sank in the North Atlantic in April 1912 after striking an iceberg?
questions.fact: Sank on its maiden voyage from Southampton to New York City.

questions.q: Which Portuguese explorer became the first European to sail around the southernmost tip of Africa (Cape of Good Hope) in 1488?
questions.fact: Dias named it Cabo das Tormentas (Cape of Storms), later renamed Cape of Good Hope by King John II.

questions.q: In which city is the famous Leaning Tower located?
questions.fact: The freestanding bell tower of Pisa Cathedral in Italy.

questions.q: What international wall dividing an iconic European city fell on 9 November 1989, marking the end of the Cold War era?
questions.fact: The fall of the Berlin Wall reunited East and West Germany.

questions.q: Which ancient civilization built the colossal stone monument known as the Great Sphinx at Giza?
questions.fact: Carved out of limestone during the reign of Pharaoh Khafre (~2500 BC).

questions.q: How many total days did Nelson Mandela spend imprisoned before his release on 11 February 1990?
questions.fact: Mandela spent 27 years, 6 months, and 6 days (10,052 days) in prison.

questions.q: What is the official weight in metric tons of a standard full-size concrete dolos used on harbor breakwaters?
questions.fact: Standard breakwater dolosse weigh approximately 20 tons each.

questions.q: In what calendar year did the historic Apollo 11 moon landing take place?
questions.fact: July 1969.
